```console
Randomised experiments on networks suffer from interference.
A standard estimator of the global average treatment effect (GATE) regresses the outcome on own treatment and a summary of neighbours' treatments, then predicts at all-treated and all-control.
We ask how accurate it is, what determines its error and when it should not be used, treating it as extrapolation from the exposures the experiment produced to the two global corners.
In simulations with exactly known GATE (six interference mechanisms, synthetic and two real graphs, Bernoulli and cluster assignment; each combination of graph, mechanism, design and noise level is a cell), the error has two parts.
The variance follows the leverage of the corner contrast: where the model is correct, the standard deviation scales as $n^{-0.50}$ and $(1{+}d)^{0.55}$ in sample size and mean degree.
The bias is, on our reading, the response's curvature times the distance to the corners, which data inside the observed range cannot identify; a formula that knows the true response matches the measured bias in 87\% of cells, but how the bias depends on degree differs by mechanism.
Regression beats difference-in-means in most cells; the spillover share above which it wins rises with degree, and a threshold mechanism is the exception on synthetic graphs but not on real ones.
Two expectations fail: no data-computable score we tried predicts the bias usefully, and nominal 95\% intervals cover only 74\% of Bernoulli cells.
Flexible learners do not beat the regression except under the threshold mechanism.
All outcomes are simulated, and shares describe our grid.

shown.message:
I haven't pushed a new head to #10 yet. `internal-review-repo` rejected version 2 for two fixes in `figtab-repo`'s files, and I'm waiting on those before cutting the next head.

**Waiting on `figtab-repo` (opened as figtab-repo#5):**
- **Table 2:** the "R² abs." column mixes two targets. The combined-score rows (0.32, 0.34, 0.43) are R² of log RMSE, and the bias rows are R² of log |bias|. I asked `figtab-repo` to name the target per row or split the column. They should also add the held-out constant row (−0.239 on the 1224 cells) that `experiment-repo` just delivered.
- **Figure numbers:** `REPRODUCE.md` section 9 maps Fig. 9 to the cluster figure and "Fig. A9" to the oracle figure, but the paper has Fig. 9 as the fitted-form oracle and Fig. 10 as the cluster designs. `CAPTIONS.md` has no paper numbers at all. I sent the full figure and table mapping, checked against the system build.

**Pushed to `dev` (b157b0d), wording the review also flagged:**
- The Results sentence on absolute R² now includes the held-out constant (−0.24). It says S̄ and p(1−p) do no better than a constant. S_adj (−0.06) and corner × curvature (−0.12) do slightly better.
- The abstract and introduction now say 85% for the population-OLS prediction. That is the figure before the post-hoc centring, which Results reports as 86.7%.
- Flexible learners now "match" the regression on the threshold mechanism instead of beating it. The median ratios are 0.99, 1.09 and 1.02.
- A local build still ends the main text on page 9, and no references are undefined.

I commented on #12 with this. Once `figtab-repo` delivers the Table 2 fix and the `REPRODUCE.md`/`CAPTIONS.md` numbering, I'll update the Table 2 caption in `appendix.tex` to match and push the new head.

The GNN, cluster Horvitz–Thompson and P6/P7 results are still pending at `experiment-repo`, and the review wants them before the final version.
